# Independent conditional contribution review: T333Q209, ROUND1

This review assigns **conditional contribution TECHNICAL at the ENTIRE unchanged frozen scope**. The condition is full correctness of the ENTIRE unchanged FROZEN-STATEMENT.md **and the ENTIRE submitted AUTHOR-PROOF.md**, not correctness of a selected lemma or a repaired argument. **Correctness remains UNDISCHARGED in this role.** This document supplies no correctness grade, acceptance decision, or count. The parent alone adopts decisions.

The conclusion is based on a complete compatible construction, given below, rather than on failure of a linear inverse at the Clifford torus, labels attached to the author's operations, an inaccessible reference, or a literature-priority claim. The author performed real calculations and quantitative organization. After paying the stipulated Source333 construction, the eligible original r107 operations, and ordinary quadratic splitting and finite coefficient matching, I find no additional substantial nonroutine operation in this particular whole target. This is a project contribution classification; it does not assert that an earlier publication states the identical theorem or the integer 88k+54.

The unchanged target has every m>=2, k=max(10,2m+2), r=88k+54, the entire small C^r ball of smooth metric perturbations of g0, an O(||h||_C^r^(1/2)) C^m bound at the fixed Clifford embedding into R4, a smooth globally injective realization, h=0, both signs and zero mean shear, and the exact integral and C1 lower bounds. None of these clauses is dropped. No selection in h, simultaneous estimates for all m on one selected map, or finite-regularity extension is added. The submitted statement and proof are preserved byte-for-byte in private scope copies; their original SHA256 values are 9008ac4ac426a6ff7f4419aaab3f6dcd0e48b73b3186f53b0122b3ab3248091a and 57ae02af6e6441b170e4a1173bb97b043b952476172277639e37a345666632c5.

## 1. What is paid and what must be compared

Source333 at fd4aeeb2ee4fc729c18d98444fed42fd0529eeeb, including its operative proofs, is stipulated true. I authenticated all 14 supplied blobs against the complete pinned tree and read all nine operative included TeX bodies, the wrapper, README, bibliography, and figure TeX. In particular, the paid input is much stronger than its headline global immersion theorem or its displayed R=440 exact-correction proposition. It includes arbitrary finite accuracy in small modes, finite weighted-input dependence, the step for every k>=10, an all-order linear recurrence, and the finite waiting-time schedule. The source is not being audited here.

The exact original r107 scope and complete sections 2–6 are also paid. That scope is smooth isometric embedding of every closed orientable smooth Riemannian surface into R4, without a prescribed nearby map or this quantitative stability estimate. Its proof supplies compact C1 embedding openness, the oblique tubular projection with differential annihilating a chosen complementary plane field, transversality of the velocity plane to the old tangent plane, and control of the projected perturbed map. It also assembles finite primitive stages and handles disconnected components by translation. These are credited explicitly; global embedding by itself is not new here. This review uses the simpler C1 openness consequence once the quantitative construction stays near F0.

The genuinely relevant comparison is whether the approximate map and the uniform exact-correction initialization require an operation beyond these paid mechanisms and elementary singular quadratic algebra. Sections 2–6 carry that comparison with the complete derivative budget and constants' dependencies. Section 7 compares actual primary mechanisms, including perturbed and singular routes; it does not merely reject a headline theorem at F0.

## 2. Periodic splitting and the entire scalar interval

Write n1=(cos x,sin x,0,0), e1=(-sin x,cos x,0,0), n2=(0,0,cos y,sin y), e2=(0,0,-sin y,cos y). Set

    U=u1 e1+u2 e2+v1 n1+v2 n2,
    gamma(F0+U)-g0=L U+B(U,U).

Here B(U,V)11=<Ux,Vx>, B(U,V)22=<Uy,Vy>, and B(U,V)12=(<Ux,Vy>+<Uy,Vx>)/2. Thus B costs one derivative in C^s product estimates. Direct differentiation gives

    (LU)11=2(partial_x u1+v1),
    (LU)12=partial_y u1+partial_x u2,
    (LU)22=2(partial_y u2+v2).

Let ell(A)=(4 pi^2)^(-1) integral A12. The range of L is exactly ker ell. For A in this kernel, use the zero-mean periodic inverse of Delta and put

    u1=partial_y Delta^(-1) A12,  u2=partial_x Delta^(-1) A12,
    v1=A11/2-partial_x u1,        v2=A22/2-partial_y u2.

Call the resulting map P A. Then LP A=A. The Fourier multipliers in this formula have order at most zero, apart from the harmless fixed frame derivatives. Bounding Fourier coefficients by C^(s+4) derivatives and summing (1+|n|)^(-4) on Z² gives

    ||P A||_C^s <= p_s ||A||_C^(s+4).

The deliberately loose loss four is uniform on the full tensor ball. It is not an assumed periodic right inverse on tensors of nonzero mean shear. Fourier projection E with E12=E21=1, E11=E22=0 gives Pi A=A-ell(A)E; both Pi and ell have fixed norm bounds.

For any periodic phi define

    V_phi=phi_x e1-phi_y e2-phi_xx n1+phi_yy n2.

Then LV_phi=0. For phi=cos(px+qy), with theta=px+qy, the derivatives in the ordered frame (n1,e1,n2,e2) are

    (V_phi)x=(p(1-p²)sin theta, 0, p q² sin theta, p q cos theta),
    (V_phi)y=(-p² q sin theta, -p q cos theta, q(q²-1)sin theta, 0).

Consequently

    ell B(V_phi,V_phi)=(pq/2)[p²(p²-1)+q²(q²-1)].

Take V+=V_cos(2x+y)/sqrt(12), V-=V_cos(2x-y)/sqrt(12). Their quadratic values are +1 and -1. Their mixed ell-pairing is zero: after taking the dot products in the common orthonormal frame, products of the distinct Fourier frequencies have zero integral.

For a normalized tensor H with ||H||_C^0<=1, c=ell H lies in [-1,1]. Put

    a=sqrt(1+c/2), b=sqrt(1-c/2), W=a V+ + b V-.

Then LW=0, ell B(W,W)=a²-b²=c, and

    2 ell B(W,V+)=2a >= sqrt(2).

All derivatives of W in the spatial variables are uniformly bounded. This resolves both signs and c=0 with a denominator separated from zero. At c=0 one deliberately uses a nonzero null vector V++V- of the indefinite quadratic form. The construction never divides by sqrt(|c|), so a sequence with arbitrarily small or zero mean shear causes no loss of uniformity.

This is the elementary indefinite quadratic submersion away from its vertex. To expose the compatible singular-inverse operation explicitly, write

    U=epsilon W+epsilon²(PY+d V+),  Y in ker ell.

After division of the range equation by epsilon² and the scalar equation by epsilon³ (the scalar coefficient of epsilon² already equals c), their leading equations are

    Y+Pi B(W,W)=Pi H,
    2 ell B(W,PY)+2a d=0.

The triangular inverse for increments (Z,e) is Y=Z and d=(e-2 ell B(W,PZ))/(2a). It has fixed finite derivative loss and a uniform scalar denominator. The remaining terms are explicit polynomials with positive powers of epsilon. This proves the needed normalized quadratic operation directly. It neither assumes a full inverse of Dgamma(F0) nor assumes, without verification, an exact right inverse at a perturbed map. Only a finite polynomial expansion is needed before the paid exact correction.

## 3. Finite matching, including uniform derivative dependence

Set W1=W. Choose provisional W2=P(H-B(W1,W1)); the argument of P has zero ell. For j=3,...,J, suppose lower coefficients have already been fixed, with W_(j-1) provisional. Form

    Zj=sum_(a+b=j, a,b>=1) B(Wa,Wb).

Its dependence on the still adjustable W_(j-1) is exactly 2B(W1,W_(j-1)). Set

    beta_j=-ell(Zj)/(2a),
    W_(j-1) <- W_(j-1)+beta_j V+,
    Wj=-P(Zj+2 beta_j B(W1,V+)).

The changed coefficient remains in the same L-fiber. Its first quadratic effect is at degree j. Its square first occurs at degree 2j-2>j for j>=3. Thus no previously matched coefficient is changed. The tensor supplied to P has zero ell. Induction matches the coefficient of epsilon² to H and all coefficients of degrees 3,...,J to zero. WJ need not be finalized at degree J+1 because the required residual starts there.

Here are the derivative counts rather than an appeal to a formal-series theorem. A product B costs one derivative, P costs at most four, and the scalar correction can use a C1 norm of the preceding coefficient even when the requested output is C0. Inductively, a provisional coefficient Wj in C^s uses at most C^(s+6j-1) of H; a finalized coefficient uses at most C^(s+6j). For the inductive step, B requires the previously constructed coefficients at s+5 before application of P. A preceding index at most j-1 therefore uses no more than s+5+6(j-1)=s+6j-1 derivatives. At scalar finalization the observation order zero may require one extra derivative, which is covered by the reserved sixth derivative. W1 is a fixed finite combination controlled by |c|<=1. Scalar division is by 2a>=sqrt(2). The remaining estimates use only fixed-mode norms, p_s, finite product constants, and earlier coefficients. Finite induction gives constants depending on s,J alone for all normalized H in the stated finite ball.

In particular, for every finite R,J, if ||H||_C^(R+2+6J)<=1 and 0<epsilon<=1, the finite smooth map

    f=F0+sum_(j=1)^J epsilon^j Wj

satisfies, for a fixed A_(R,J),

    ||f-F0||_C^(R+2) <= A_(R,J) epsilon,
    ||gamma(f)-(g0+epsilon² H)||_C^R <= A_(R,J) epsilon^(J+1).

The residual is a finite sum through degree 2J. No convergence of a power series, inverse on an infinite scale, bound on all derivatives of H, or selection regularity is being assumed. This is finite coefficient matching in a quadratic map with a split range and one regularized scalar direction. Källén's finite substitutions and the small-mode substitutions already paid in Source333 are relevant antecedent operations; the present Fourier coefficients and the loose six-per-stage budget are author-specific algebra, not a new inverse theorem.

## 4. The complete Source333 operation used for exact correction

The source's construction cannot be replaced in this comparison by the sentence “apply Nash–Moser.” Its operative content is as follows.

First, its primitive and global sections build local velocity loops in the normal/velocity plane, remove transverse metric components algebraically, preserve a nonzero second fundamental form in a selected direction, and decompose positive tensors with positive coefficients on finitely many local phase squares. Rotated covector triples and a partition by squares provide positive decomposition margins. A finite hierarchy of phase weights keeps pairwise sum and difference phases admissible. The geometry-preservation and global-construction sections retain these margins through finite primitive stages; these operations and their finite derivative dependence are paid. For the present comparison one may fix all such phase data at F0 and g0 once. The nonzero second fundamental form of F0 and strict decomposition margins persist in a fixed C² neighborhood. No target-dependent shrinking phase neighborhood is necessary.

For completeness, the small-mode proof eliminates the normal yy component using the nonzero normal vector B_yy. The remaining oscillatory equations reduce to (i/tau+L)u=k for a first-order slow-coefficient operator. A finite residual iteration with its principal inverse gains tau/s per repetition; at accuracy q it has a finite derivative requirement depending on q. The free normal direction perpendicular to B_yy produces the leading positive quadratic mean delta² sum a_nu² dphi_nu². The induced finite mean-coefficient map has the form A+T(A), with T small at the scale ratio. Repeated substitutions A_(i+1)=H-T(A_i) reduce its error to the chosen finite order. Doubled phases and pairwise sums/differences account for the other quadratic terms; the secondary oscillatory corrections cancel them. Every operation is finite and local with specified cutoffs. The result used here, in the source's unperturbed case, is

    |U|_(l,tau) <= C_l delta tau,
    |E|_(l,tau) <= C_l[delta(tau/s)^q+delta³/tau].

The constants and scale threshold use finitely many weighted derivatives of the smoothed inputs, phase data and margins. In the more general polynomially perturbed version the auxiliary exponent can be chosen p=E+6 independently of q; it is not needed to insert an uncontrolled background perturbation into the present unperturbed application. Neither version requires a full periodic linear right inverse at F0. Frequency nonresonance, amplitude inversion, and the exact weighted dependence are paid proof operations, not new labels to be credited to this nominee.

Define, for a smooth current map G and normalized defect H,

    S_l(t;G,H)=sum_(j=0)^l t^j (||G||_C^(j+2)+||H||_C^j).

Smoothing by kernels whose moments through order r vanish is a finite Vandermonde construction. If S_r<=B, then for 0<tau<=s<=t<=1 the source proves, at every fixed observation order l,

    |j²G_s|_(l,s)+|H_s|_(l,s) <= C_(l,r) B,
    |j²(G-G_s)|_(l,tau)+|H-H_s|_(l,tau)
      <= C_(l,r)[B(s/t)^r+S_l(t)(tau/t)^r].

For derivative orders j<=r the Taylor remainder is bounded by B t^(-r) s^(r-j) tau^j. For j>r boundedness of smoothing gives (tau/t)^j S_l. This is the exact split that keeps unknown high derivatives linear and confines all finite mode-formula demands to smoothed inputs. The mode formulas can ask for arbitrarily large but finite orders as q increases: the first displayed smoothed bound supplies them without increasing the initial true-input order. This point is essential to the full finite C^r ball.

Take any k>=10 and use the source scales

    beta=6/5, lambda=11/10, tau=t^beta, s=t^lambda,
    delta=t^k, r(k)=q(k)=40(k+1),
    delta'=tau^k or tau^(k+1).

The fixed-reference bridge is an exact algebraic substitution. Let g denote the actual target metric, independently of the fixed reference g0, and put H=delta^(-2)(g-gamma(G)). Apply the small-mode construction at G_s to H_s-(delta'/delta)²g0. Define its metric error by

    E=gamma(G_s+U)-gamma(G_s)-delta²[H_s-(delta'/delta)²g0].

Add U to the unsmoothed G. For H'=delta'^(-2)(g-gamma(G+U)), expansion of the quadratic metric gives

    delta'²(H'-g0)=delta²(H-H_s)-E-C(G-G_s,U),
    C(V,W)ij=<partial_i V,partial_j W>+<partial_j V,partial_i W>.

The target g cancels exactly. There is no square of the smoothing tail. Only derivatives of the fixed reference g0 occur outside H; its coordinate entries are constant. Positivity is required for the small-mode input near g0, not for H with an uncontrolled high-norm bound. C0 closeness, the smoothing tail estimate and delta'/delta ->0 place that input in the same positive-decomposition neighborhood. This is the source error identity with its two uses of the reference separated, not an extra nonlinear existence operation.

For the more demanding choice delta'=tau^(k+1), the six divided error terms and exponents are

| Term before division by delta'² | Exponent of t afterward |
| --- | --- |
| delta(tau/s)^q | (13k+8)/5 |
| delta³/tau | (3k-18)/5 |
| delta² B(s/t)^r | (18k+8)/5 |
| delta² S_l(tau/t)^r | (38k+28)/5 |
| delta B(s/t)^r | (13k+8)/5 |
| delta S_l(tau/t)^r | (33k+28)/5 |

They follow by inserting r=q=40(k+1), beta=6/5 and lambda=11/10, and all exceed 1/5 for k>=10. The larger choice delta'=tau^k is easier. Positive weighted orders inherited from G gain tau/t=t^(1/5); |j²U|_(l,tau)<=C delta/tau. Thus, with fixed phase data and a fixed B, the complete source recurrence becomes

    S_l(tau;G+U,H')
      <= ||G||_C²+||g0||_C0+C_(l,k) t^(1/5)(1+S_l(t;G,H)),
    |H'-g0|_(l,tau)<=C_(l,k)t^(1/5)(1+S_l).

Constants depend on l,k,B, fixed norms/atlas/smoothing, and the fixed phase neighborhood and margins. They do not depend on higher true derivatives of g. Choose B so that the baseline is <B/4 throughout that neighborhood. This replaces the source's z-dependent B and rho by constants, which is legitimate because the present approximate maps are uniformly close to one fixed F0. It improves the bookkeeping rather than changing the correction mechanism.

## 5. Exact constants, finite initial input, and the smooth limit

Fix m>=2. Put k0=max(10,2m+2), R=40(k0+1), and J=8k0+2. The finite matching input order is exactly

    R+2+6J=40k0+40+2+48k0+12=88k0+54=r_m.

Let epsilon=||h||_C^r_m^(1/2). If epsilon=0 use F0. Otherwise H=h/epsilon² has C^r_m norm one, with no condition whatsoever on its higher norms. Section 3 produces f with ||f-F0||_C^(R+2)<=A_m epsilon and e=gamma(f)-g bounded by A_m epsilon^(J+1) in C^R, where g=g0+h. The constants A_m depend only on the displayed integer orders and the fixed operators and frames. The finite-stage maps are smooth because h is smooth; this does not bound their higher norms uniformly.

Initialize the exact scheme at

    t0=epsilon^4, delta0=t0^k0=epsilon^(4k0),
    G0=sqrt(1-delta0²) f.

The normalized defect identity is

    H0=delta0^(-2)(g-gamma(G0))
      =g+(1-delta0^(-2))e.

Since J+1-8k0=3, H0-g0=O_C^R(epsilon²+epsilon³). G0 is uniformly bounded in C^(R+2), and its displacement from f is O_C^m(epsilon^(8k0)). Consequently S_R(t0;G0,H0)<=B/2 after a threshold depending only on m and the fixed A_m. This uses only the frozen finite input bound. The initial approximate map and G0 lie in the chosen fixed C² phase neighborhood.

At each step impose in addition

    ||U||_C^floor(k/2) <= epsilon³ t.

This is available from the increment estimate because its unweighted exponent is

    e_k=k+(6/5)(1-floor(k/2))>1.

For the initial block, all constants are uniform and the inequalities are finite in number. Moreover 4(e_k0-1)>3, so t0=epsilon^4 makes C t0^(e_k0-1)<=epsilon³ uniformly for small epsilon. This verifies, rather than assumes, that the chosen initial scale can meet the stronger displacement target. At later blocks epsilon is fixed; their scale thresholds may depend on it and on the block order, while the initial smallness threshold still depends only on m. These later thresholds introduce no extra input norm in eta_m.

Replace t by t^(6/5) at every step. Thus t_n=t0^((6/5)^n), and sum_n t_n<1/4 for sufficiently small t0. Since floor(k0/2)>=m, every increment is controlled in C^m. Their C² sum keeps the entire iteration in the fixed phase neighborhood. The C0 normalized defect stays near g0, and the controlled S_r(k) bound is preserved by the recurrence at r(k), with the baseline <B/4.

The passage to all derivatives is not inferred from estimates at a single finite order. Hold k fixed and consider any observation order l. Smoothness of finite stages gives finite x_n=S_l(t_n;G_n,H_n), possibly extremely large. The paid all-order recurrence says

    x_(n+1)<=B/4+c_n(1+x_n), c_n=C_(l,k)t_n^(1/5)->0.

Once c_n<=1/4 the sequence is bounded by the elementary affine contraction estimate. Thereafter c_n->0 gives limsup x_n<=B/4. In particular x_n<=B eventually. Apply this with l=r(k+1). Wait until that bound holds, the scale is below the next block's threshold, and C_(r(k+1),k)t^(1/5)(1+B)<=B/2. Each waiting time is finite. Make the transition with delta'=tau^(k+1); the recurrence, already proved for this harder amplitude, yields the new controlled norm <3B/4. Continue. Thus every k is reached after finitely many steps and k tends to infinity.

For every fixed l, eventually floor(k/2)>=l, so the tail is absolutely summable in C^l. The limit is smooth. Its metric is g, since the actual defect is delta²H, H remains bounded in C0, delta->0, and metric evaluation is continuous in C1. High derivatives of h affect only finite waiting times, not the initial ball, the exponent, the bound in the requested C^m, or the derivative order r_m.

Finally,

    ||F-f||_C^m <= A_m epsilon^(8k0)+epsilon³ sum_n t_n,
    ||F-F0||_C^m <= A_m epsilon+A_m epsilon^(8k0)+epsilon³/4.

After epsilon<=1 and increasing the finite constant, this is C_m epsilon. One may take, for example, C_m=2A_m+1 with A_m enlarged to cover the finite map and initial rescaling estimates. Choose eta_m=epsilon_m², where epsilon_m is the minimum of the finitely many initial thresholds above, 1, and a fixed C1 embedding-openness radius divided by C_m. These constants depend only on m and the fixed conventions. No numerical value for C_m or eta_m is asserted by the frozen theorem; their quantified dependencies, and the exact integers 88 and 54, are what must be retained. Positivity of g is assumed in the target and is also ensured by a sufficiently small C0 perturbation; no smaller ball involving infinitely many derivatives is used.

## 6. Global embedding and the exact lower bound

Compact C1 openness, explicitly proved in the admitted original r107 construction, applies to F0. To recall its content: on sufficiently small coordinate neighborhoods the derivative of F0 has a uniformly injective projection to its tangent plane, and this persists for C1-close maps, giving local injectivity. A finite cover handles all sufficiently close pairs. On the compact complement of those pairs the injective F0 has a strictly positive separation, which persists under C0 perturbation. The derivative remains injective as well. Thus a sufficiently small C1 neighborhood consists of embeddings. Taking epsilon_m small in section 5 gives a smooth global embedding, with the very same quantitative bound. No unresolved global self-intersection elimination or extra ambient dimension is inserted.

The oblique-projection argument of r107 is stronger in a different direction: if a perturbation has a large velocity-plane term, its tubular projection kills that term and makes the projected map C1-close to the old embedding. Its plane-field extension, transverse condition, mean-zero primitive, and finite-stage global assembly are paid. They are not claimed as a new feature of this nominee, even though the present small C1 construction only needs their simpler openness lemma.

For the frozen shear metric, the mixed entry of gamma(F0+U) is

    partial_y u1+partial_x u2+<Ux,Uy>=t.

This identity holds for C1 maps using the smooth periodic frame. Periodic integration eliminates the first two terms and gives

    integral_T² <Ux,Uy>=4 pi² t.

Hence

    8 pi² |t| <= integral_T² (|Ux|²+|Uy|²).

Also |t|<=sup|Ux| sup|Uy|<=||U||_C1², proving the exact lower bound ||U||_C1>=sqrt(|t|). No immersion, injectivity, or higher regularity is used in this obstruction. For the specified coordinate tensor norm, ||h_t||_C^r=|t| for every finite r, and g0+h_t is positive when |t|<1. If an exponent alpha>1/2 worked on any such full ball, sqrt(|t|)<=C|t|^alpha would fail as t->0. The argument covers both signs, and t=0 gives the stated zero lower bound. This is the elementary integral obstruction paired with the same scalar quadratic range calculation, not a further substantial operation.

## 7. Actual primary comparisons and the strongest compatible routes

The comparison here is constructive. A method need not work at F0 itself: a perturbation of size O(epsilon), an inverse with an epsilon-dependent bound, and a sufficiently accurate finite residual could in principle compose to exactly the frozen estimate. The mean-zero range of L alone cannot exclude such a route. Sections 2–5 actually implement the needed quadratic desingularization, finite approximation and smooth completion without requiring an unproved exact full inverse. The following primary evidence explains which classical operations are paid and which hypotheses cannot simply be omitted.

**Nash (1956), original paper.** The rendered pages read include Part A's smoothing construction and the free-map algebra, together with the printed theorem on p.52. The free algebra solves the equations obtained by adding <partial_i F,U>=0 and differentiating: first and symmetric second derivatives must be independent. For n=2 this is five vectors. No map into R4, perturbed or otherwise, can satisfy this free-map condition. This excludes only that particular algebraic free inverse in this ambient dimension. Nash's smoothing and finite-error mechanisms are still compatible and are already embodied in Source333. The entire Part B estimate proof was not read, and this review does not claim to have verified Nash's whole paper or to derive the target from its headline embedding theorem.

**Källén (1978), original paper.** The operative finite substitutions are actual proof steps, not just a theorem name. The primitive tensor decomposition has positive coefficient margins; Lemmas 2.2–2.3 invert the finite amplitude map by an ordinary parameter-dependent finite-dimensional implicit construction. Lemma 3.3 repeatedly substitutes coefficients, estimating successive errors and using one more derivative per correction stage. These operations explain why a finite algebraic approximate inverse, with deliberately oversized derivative reserves, is routine even though an infinite unsmoothed iteration would lose derivatives. Källén's stated ambient dimensions and Hölder endpoint are not substituted for the present R4 smooth theorem. The compatible operation is finite matching followed by the stronger stipulated source completion. The particular two Fourier modes and the constants here are attributed to the author, without treating their explicitness as substantial by itself.

**Moser (1966), original Chapter I, §5.** The actually readable equations require, near each current u, approximate solutions v of F'(u)v=g with a residual controlled by a negative power of the approximation parameter, a norm bound with a positive power, and a quadratic nonlinear remainder estimate. The proof then chooses rapidly growing smoothing parameters and interpolates to achieve summability. A bounded right inverse at one base point, or only the mean-zero part of a derivative, is not this hypothesis. Conversely Moser allows an approximate inverse mechanism; one cannot dismiss all such mechanisms merely because L at F0 has a cokernel. In this reduction the required approximation and smoothing estimates are supplied concretely by the finite matching and the source formulas in sections 3–5, with all true-input dependence shown. The Moser extraction omits equations, so the hypotheses and the selected theorem's proof were read in page renders. No reliance is placed on missing OCR formulas.

**Gromov (1986), original book, and Gromov (2015), original essay.** The book was obtained during this independent review, after an initial bounded download was too small; this removes the author's book-access limit for the portions actually read. The book's §§2.3.1–2.3.3 specify a differential inverse L_x M_x=Id on an open jet relation, smoothly dependent on x, and describe the smoothed Newton error telescope. Its §2.3.8 generic-operator proof passes to formal adjoints so that left inversion is a finite linear algebraic system in jet coefficients. Rational solutions give an open set; the proof increases the order using transverse noncharacteristic directions and polynomial identities to raise the codimension of the exceptional jets. These are genuine perturbed-operator mechanisms, stronger than an inversion test solely at F0.

The same book explicitly treats the non-free metric problem in §2.3.8(E'): introducing auxiliary h_i converts the five equations into a differential compatibility system. The coefficients of that system are constrained by being derivatives of a map; the generic theorem for arbitrary operators cannot be applied without that compatibility analysis. The read 2015 essay likewise states infinitesimal inversion with derivative defect/order, its nonlinear regularity requirements, and extensions to suitable nonlocal inverses. Neither source licenses equating full second-derivative rank with a periodic right inverse.

I also read the book's non-free discussion in §3.1.9 and its low-codimension constructions in §3.2.4. These contain stronger actual constructions than a free-map headline. In particular, the torus R4 immersion argument uses warped products, conformal classes, a normalized elliptic equation and flat tori obtained through the Hopf construction. The stability/decomposition argument for R5 perturbs a stable decomposition to a strongly stable one before replacing a primitive term by a sine/cosine pair. The elliptic equation in Proposition (B) is a perturbation of the Laplacian on normalized functions/mean-zero forms, with finite-dimensional conformal parameters. These classical mechanisms are credited. They are not silently asserted to provide a quantitative selection near this prescribed Clifford embedding: the Hopf/conformal construction permits a different base immersion, and the strongly stable R5 construction uses another ambient dimension. Their existence does not obstruct a stronger composed route; here the exact missing local algebra is instead furnished explicitly in sections 2–3, with the finite residual and source completion. No uninspected book section is used as a premise.

**D’Ambra–Loi (2007), newly obtained original.** The entire eight-page paper was read. Besides independence of f_x,f_y,f_xx,f_yy, its construction requires independence of two compatibility vector fields and nonvanishing of an additional differential expression. Writing the compatibility operators as Lhat_i=L_i+A_i and [L1,L2]=r1 L1+r2 L2, the expression is

    Dhat=Lhat1(r1)+Lhat2(r2)-L1(A2)+L2(A1).

When Dhat is nonzero, the proof takes x1=r1 ghat/Dhat, x2=r2 ghat/Dhat, x3=-ghat/Dhat; then h1=x1+Lhat2 x3 and h2=x2-Lhat1 x3 solve the compatibility equation. This is an explicit differential inverse, with denominators and their derivatives. parameter derivative is needed: this proves strict concavity pointwise.

## Exact source target

Li Yin, Li-Guo Huang, Yong-Li Wang and Xiu-Li Lin, *A survey for generalized
trigonometric and hyperbolic functions*, Journal of Mathematical Inequalities
13(3) (2019), 833–854, DOI 10.7153/jmi-2019-13-58, Conjecture 5.1 on printed
p.847: for fixed 0<x<1, p -> arcsinh_p(x) is strictly concave on (1,infinity).
The defining integral is (1.14):

    A(p,x) = integral_0^x (1+t^p)^(-1/p) dt.

This is the narrower surviving formulation identified in the earlier
pi-arcsinh-concavity-preliminary-review, whose small-p witness did not answer
it. That review wrongly attributed the survey to other authors; the actual
title page gives the four names above. The original Baricz–Bhayo–Vuorinen,
Filomat 29(2) (2015), 303–313, Conjecture 2.4, used all p>0 and is false
there by the old uncredited witness. These source questions must be separated.

## Proposed stronger theorem

For every x>0, the literal integral A(p,x) is strictly concave on
(log(2)/2,infinity). In particular it answers the entire 2019 Conjecture 5.1.
No assertion that this is the optimal parameter interval for A is made.

## Proof

For u>0 define

    H(u) = log(1+u) - u log(u)/(1+u).

Writing r=u/(1+u) in (0,1) gives

    H(u) = -r log(r) -(1-r) log(1-r) >0.

Furthermore H'(u)=-log(u)/(1+u)^2. Thus H increases up to u=1 and decreases
afterwards, so H(u)<=H(1)=log(2). This is the elementary binary-entropy bound;
it is classical and is not claimed as a new tool or outcome.

Fix t>0, and put u=t^p, f(p,t)=(1+t^p)^(-1/p), ell=log f. For p>0,

    ell_p = H(u)/p^2,
    dH(t^p)/dp = -p (log t)^2 u/(1+u)^2,
    ell_pp = -2H(u)/p^3 -(log t)^2 u/[p(1+u)^2].

Consequently the exact second derivative is

    f_pp = f/p^4 * [ H(u)^2 -2p H(u)
                           -p^3 (log t)^2 u/(1+u)^2 ].

For p>log(2)/2, we have 0<H(u)<=log(2)<2p. Hence H(u)^2-2pH(u)<0,
and the final term in the bracket is nonpositive. Thus f_pp<0 for every
t>0 and every p>log(2)/2. No interchange of an improper integral and a
parameter derivative is needed: this proves strict concavity pointwise.

For distinct p0,p1 in this interval and 0<lambda<1, the strict pointwise
Jensen inequality holds for every t>0. At t=0 the integrand is exactly 1,
so the corresponding non-strict inequality holds there. Each integrand is
continuous on [0,x] for p>0. The Jensen gap is continuous and positive on
(0,x]; for instance it is positive at x/2. Its integral is therefore
strictly positive. Integration of the Jensen inequality proves

    A(lambda*p0+(1-lambda)*p1,x)
      > lambda*A(p0,x)+(1-lambda)*A(p1,x).

This is strict concavity on the stated interval. Since log(2)/2<1, it
implies exactly the 2019 source statement for 0<x<1 and p>1. Positivity
then gives the source's strict multiplicative Turan consequence for p>2.
This consequence is not a separate outcome.
